summary: Takeo Hibino was a scholar of sinology, history, and archaeology who studied at Kyoto University (~1933–1936). He held posts at the Academy of Oriental Culture's Kyoto Institute, Kyoto University (1948–1977), Otemon Gakuin University, and Otemae University.
Takeo Izumi specializes in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Tohoku University (~1973–1981) and later served there as a professor (~1997–2018).

Takeo Kanaseki was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1919–1923). He held academic posts at Kyushu University (~1949–1960), Tottori University (~1960–1965), and Tezukayama Gakuin University (~1965–1979).
Takeo Kuwabara was a philosophy scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1925–1928). He later held posts at Tohoku University (~1931–1948) and served as a professor at Kyoto University (~1948–1968).

Takeshi Fujii is a historian and Indologist who studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and the University of Delhi. He spent his academic career at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies from 1987, becoming professor and later professor emeritus in 2021.

Takeshi Hasegawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a post at Ryukoku University (attested 1998) and served as a lecturer at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Takeshi Karashima was a Sinologist who studied at Yamaguchi Higher School and Tokyo Imperial University (~1923–1926). His career included positions at Keijo Imperial University (~1931–1945), Sagami Women's University (~1951–1967), Showa Women's University, and Kamakura's library.

Takeshi Umehara was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology who studied at Kyoto University under Tokuryu Yamauchi and Michitaro Tanaka. He held posts at Ritsumeikan University, Kyoto City University of Arts, and the International Research Center for Japanese Studies.

Takeshiro Kuraishi was a scholar of Sinology and linguistics who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1925–1928). He served as a professor at Kyoto University (~1939–1949) and held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1958).

Takezo Kaneko was a philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji (~1928–1931). He taught at Hokkaido University, the University of Tokyo (~1947–1966), International Christian University, and Seikei University.
Taklung Tsetrul Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied under Po Lu Khenpo Dorjé. He taught Phakchok Rinpoche and succeeded Trulshik Rinpoche in 2012.
Taku Fukuda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Hajime Sakurabe (~1986–1993). He has held positions at Doho University, Nagoya University, and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Takudo Ishikawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He held a research post at the Jodo Shu Research Institute (attested 2005) and teaching posts at Taisho University (attested 2015 and 2026).

Takushu Sugimoto is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at Tohoku University. He held professorships at Kanazawa University (~1986–2001, emeritus ~2001), Komazawa University (attested 1990), and Kinjo University (~2001–2006).

Tampalawela Dhammaratana is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Kelaniya, University of Paris under Jean-François Lyotard, Paris-Sorbonne University under Michel Hulin, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat.

Tan Chung was a Sinologist and historian who earned his PhD at Visva-Bharati University. He served as Professor of Chinese at the University of Delhi (~1971–1978) and department head at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1978–1994).

Tan Poh Beng is a scholar of Buddhist studies who completed a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Charles Willemen and Tilak Kariyawasam, also studying under Gallelle Sumanasiri and Shengshou.
Tan Sitong was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied under Yang Wenhui (~1896–1898) and Wang Zhengyi.

Tan Yun-shan was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied under Taixu and Kshitimohan Sen, among others. He co-founded Visva-Bharati University, serving there as Professor of Chinese Studies (~1937–1968).
Tanaya Afroz is a linguistics scholar who studied under doctoral supervisor Shyam Sundar Bhattacharya and held a post as a research scholar/fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).
